content.rendered:
Bruce Springsteen’s 2006 Seeger Sessions Tour is remembered primarily for its mix of vintage American folk songs and inspired re-arrangements of Bruce’s original songs.

But every now and then, Bruce sprinkled a third category into the mix: a cover of a more recent popular country or rock song that fit the tour’s theme or the band’s sound.

One of the very first of these was “Long Black Veil,” originally recorded and released in 1959 by Lefty Frizzell.

“Long Black Veil” is the story of a man falsely accused of murder who goes to his grave rather than own up to his alibi (he was having an affair with his best friend’s wife at the time of the murder). His lover keeps their secret but visits his grave in the dark of night, cloaked in a long black veil.

It was a story destined for a folk song immortalization, and Frizzell’s original (which peaked at #6 on the Billboard Hot Country and Western chart) has been covered countless times, most notably by The Band (who recorded it on their debut album and performed it at Woodstock), Sammi Smith (who scored a Top 40 Country hit with it in 1974), and of course, the memorable television performance by Johnny Cash and Joni Mitchell on the very first episode of The Johnny Cash Show in 1969.

Bruce worked up a full-band arrangement of “Long Black Veil” before the Seeger Session Tour even began. At the final rehearsal show, four days before the tour officially opened at the New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival, Bruce and the Sessions Band took the stage and opened with Frizzell’s classic.

While the song didn’t make Bruce’s Jazz Fest set, he debuted it a week later in London, early in the tour’s first European leg. “Long Black Veil” would go on to make a total of ten appearances that year, each one a showcase for the spectacular vocal and musical talent arrayed across the stage.

Here’s Bruce’s final performance of “Long Black Veil” to date, live in Rome late in the Seeger Sessions Tour.

Long Black Veil
First performed: April 26, 2006 (Asbury Park, NJ)
Last performed: October 10, 2006 (Rome, Italy)

© February 5, 2020

excerpt.rendered: Lefty Frizzell’s 1959 tale of a falsely accused man who accepts his sentence rather than confess his secret was a natural temptation for a Bruce Springsteen cover treatment. Watch one of its frequent outings on Bruce’s 2006 Seeger Sessions Tour inside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cover Me, Black Veil Brides: American Skin (41 Shots)
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Black Veils Brides covered "American Skin (41 Shots)" in the wake of George Floyd's murder, and they've been performing it live ever since.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Roll of the Dice: Fade to Black
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This Nebraska-era demo uses cinematic vocabulary to devastating effect.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Black Ladder
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce and Nils accompany Elvis Costello in a tender reading of Patti Scialfa's gorgeous "Black Ladder."

jetpack-related-posts.title: Roll of the Dice: Goin’ Cali
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: "Goin' Cali" traces Bruce's journey from east to west, from isolation and frustration to connection and reinvention.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Roll of the Dice: Blood Brothers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In any version, in any arrangement, "Blood Brothers" packs an emotional punch and holds a special place in fans' hearts.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Mean Woman Blues
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce backs Roy Orbison and an all-star band on an Elvis cover that one-ups The King.
